request.spec:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the
tree receives the next number after the last number given anywhere in the tree (numbers given before
this stay as they are). Per-period numbering stays per sheet.

The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the

agent.result_text:
All sheets in a tree now share one number sequence, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What changed:** a single method, `Sheets.nextClaimNumber` in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/sheet/Sheets.java`.
- It finds the sheet's tree: it follows parent links up to the top sheet, then takes every sheet below that one.
- The new number is one more than the highest last number on any sheet in that tree. That number is stored as the opening sheet's own last number.
- Every way of opening a claim goes through this method, so they all follow the new rule.

**What doesn't change:**
- There is no database migration. Each sheet still keeps its own "last number" counter, and the tree's next number is the highest of those plus one. So numbers already given stay as they are.
- Per-period numbering (`P1-1`, `X-1`) is untouched and still counts per sheet.

**Two behaviours to be aware of:**
- **Two claims opened at the same moment** get different numbers. Opening a number locks the counters of every sheet in the tree, always in the same order, so two opens at once can't block each other.
- **A sheet linked into a tree later** gets the next number above the highest anywhere in the tree from then on. Its own earlier numbers stay as they are.
